subject.title: [Feature]:  Missing Session Management Commands in OpenClaw

question: What public session lifecycle contract should OpenClaw expose for stop, kill, pause, resume, and resource limits across Gateway, CLI, and UI?
rationale: Current main has partial abort/delete/cleanup primitives, but the requested behavior affects authorization, child-process ownership, persisted session state, UI semantics, and possible config defaults, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary.

options.title: Design Additive Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Add explicit guarded Gateway methods plus CLI/UI affordances for stop/kill/pause/resume/resource policy while preserving current abort/delete defaults and documenting upgrade behavior.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Canonical Work
options.body: Keep this umbrella open and route process kill to #12554, topic UI to #54397, resume/fork to #59109, and diagnostics to #96113 before defining any broad API.

options.title: Defer Broad Controls
options.body: Keep current abort/delete/cleanup behavior and document limitations until resource and process lifecycle ownership is designed.

recommendation.title: Design Additive Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Add explicit guarded Gateway methods plus CLI/UI affordances for stop/kill/pause/resume/resource policy while preserving current abort/delete defaults and documenting upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-main history signal across the Gateway, CLI, UI, and docs surfaces this product decision would touch.
